extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria (37 CFR 1.704 and related MPEP commentary) defining when patent term adjustment (PTA) will be reduced for applicant conduct or omissions, and what papers/conditions put an application in condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment reduction for failure to engage in reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(a) implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C)(i) and sets forth that the period of adjustment shall be reduced by a period equal to the period during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (i.e., processing or examination) of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory basis and policy: the applicant’s action or inaction need not have caused the PTO delay for PTA to be reduced; the provision creates a balance between Office delays and applicant diligence and serves the public interest in timely availability of technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for examination (required papers and fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes a specification (including at least one claim and an abstract), papers in compliance with § 1.52, drawings (if any) in compliance with § 1.84, any required English translation, a sequence listing in compliance with §§ 1.821–1.825 (if applicable), the inventor's oath/declaration or an application data sheet per § 1.63(b), the basic filing fee (§ 1.16(a) or (c)), the search fee (§ 1.16(k) or (m)), the examination fee (§ 1.16(o) or (q)), any certified copy required by § 1.57(a), and any application size fee under § 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications in national stage must include analogous items and fees (see § 1.491(b) and § 1.492). Papers/drawings/sequence listings corrected prior to mailing of an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance are considered in compliance as of the filing date of the latest correcting reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day IDS communication safe-harbor (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign or international application or by the Office that was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to the filing of the information disclosure statement (IDS) falls within the 30‑day period in § 1.704(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thirty-day period set forth is not extendable. (Context: this limits when late-received communications will be treated as applicant delay in filing an IDS.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month cumulative reply delay rule (37 CFR 1.704(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.704(b), with respect to pre-examination processing grounds (37 CFR 1.702(a)–(e)), an applicant is deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods in excess of three months taken to reply to any notice or action making any rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measured from the date the notice or action was mailed or given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of Omitted Items is not such a notice. The period of adjustment is reduced by days beginning the day after three months from mailing of the Office communication and ending on the date the reply was filed (reply filing date is actual receipt per § 1.6; certificate of mailing/transmission under § 1.8 is not counted). Applies to pre-examination notices including: Notice of Incomplete Nonprovisional Application; Notice to File Missing Parts; Notice of Informal Application; Notice to File Corrected Application Papers Filing Date Granted; Notice to Comply with Requirements for Applications Containing Sequence Disclosures. The three-month rule applies regardless of the reply period set in the Office action; examples given (e.g., two-month reply periods with available extensions, six-month secrecy order replies). If the last day falls on a weekend/holiday, filing on next business day avoids PTA reduction; examples and judicial citation (ArQule v. Kappos) provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary (non-exhaustive) list of applicant actions/inactions that interfere with Office processing (37 CFR 1.704(c) overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1)–(c)(14) set forth actions or inactions by an applicant that interfere with the Office’s ability to process or examine an application and specify how much PTA is reduced for each; the list is exemplary, not exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may also reduce PTA on the basis of other conduct that interferes with processing under authority of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C)(iii). Examples of infrequent but interfering conduct are given (e.g., meritless petitions for reconsideration, extensions for interference settlement negotiations that do not settle, claim scope changed to match examiner allowance more than six months earlier than allowance date). Applicants must refrain from actions that prevent or interfere with processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action at applicant’s request (37 CFR 1.704(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103 at the applicant’s request constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the date the request for suspension under § 1.103 was filed and ending on the date the suspension was terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of issuance at applicant’s request (37 CFR 1.704(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferral of issuance of a patent under 37 CFR 1.314 at the applicant’s request constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the date a request for deferral under § 1.314 was filed and ending on the issue date of the patent. When a petition under § 1.314 is granted, the application is generally held for a stated period and then returned to issue without further communication; the reduction covers that hold period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment or late payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.704(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of the application (by failure to prosecute) or late payment of the issue fee constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by days beginning on the date of abandonment or the day after the issue fee was due and ending on the earlier of: (1) the date of mailing of the decision reviving the application or accepting late payment; or (2) the date that is four months after the filing date of the grantable petition to revive or accept late payment. The four‑month cap is to limit the reduction if the Office does not act within four months of the grantable petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file petition to withdraw abandonment/ revive within two months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment or to revive an application within two months from the mailing date of a notice of abandonment constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant expected to file such petition within two months (see MPEP § 711.03(c)). PTA reduced by days beginning on the day after the two‑month period from mailing of the notice of abandonment and ending on the date the petition was filed. Applicants are encouraged to check PALM/PAIR records and request corrections if filings/receipts were not properly recorded; failure to request withdrawal within two months results in PTA reduction under § 1.704(c)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of provisional to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.704(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a provisional application (35 U.S.C. 111(b)) to a nonprovisional application (35 U.S.C. 111(a)) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion will require the Office to reprocess the application as a nonprovisional and can delay up to one year after the provisional filing date that would otherwise be accorded to the nonprovisional; PTA reduced by days beginning on the date the application was filed as a provisional and ending on the date a compliant request to convert under § 1.53(c)(3) was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment or paper less than one month before Office action/allowance requiring supplemental action (37 CFR 1.704(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires issuance of a supplemental Office action or notice of allowance constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA reduced by the lesser of: (a) the number of days beginning the day after the mailing date of the original Office action or notice of allowance and ending on the date of mailing of the supplemental Office action/notice of allowance; or (b) four months (a four‑month cap). The four‑month cap limits reductions if the Office takes longer to issue the supplemental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply having an omission (37 CFR 1.704(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a reply that has an omission (e.g., as covered by 37 CFR 1.135(c)) that requires the Office to issue an action indicating the omission and await a corrected reply constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA reduced by days beginning on the day after the date the reply having an omission was filed and ending on the date the correcting reply or paper was filed. The provision is not limited to § 1.135(c) actions; it also applies to notices dismissing petitions for lack of necessary items or notices that sequence listings are non-compliant. Filing of a non-compliant appeal brief will not be deemed an omission under § 1.704(c)(7) if the notice of appeal was filed on or after Sep 17, 2012 (handled under § 1.704(c)(11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply or other paper after reply (37 CFR 1.704(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper (e.g., an IDS or petition) after an initial reply has been filed that restarts consideration of the reply constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA reduced by days beginning on the day after the date the initial reply was filed and ending on the date the supplemental reply or other paper was filed. Filing such papers after an RCE but prior to a subsequent Office action is an applicant delay. This provision does not apply to papers expressly requested by the examiner; examiner-requested amendments are processed to avoid being treated as separate papers for PALM. Submissions under § 1.97(c) or amendments under § 41.33 after a notice of appeal but before PTAB jurisdiction are treated similarly as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/paper after Board/court decision less than one month before action requiring supplemental action (37 CFR 1.704(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or other paper (other than a § 41.50(c) statement) after a Patent Trial and Appeal Board decision or federal court decision, less than one month before mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, that requires a supplemental Office action/notice of allowance constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA reduced by the lesser of: (a) number of days beginning on the day after the mailing date of the original Office action or notice of allowance and ending on mailing date of the supplemental action; or (b) four months (four‑month cap). If amendment is requested by examiner, it will be processed so it is not a separate PALM-flagged paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers filed after notice of allowance that may or may not be applicant delay (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10) — exceptions and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10) treats submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper (other than an RCE under § 1.114) after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed as a circumstance constituting a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination, subject to caps and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA reduced by the lesser of: (1) number of days between filing of the amendment/other paper and the mailing date of the Office action/notice in response; or (2) four months. The MPEP lists papers that are NOT considered failures when filed after notice of allowance (fee transmittal PTOL‑85B; power of attorney; power to inspect; change of address; status changes; responses to examiner’s reasons for allowance or requests to correct errors in Notice of Allowance/Allowability; status letters; refund requests; inventor’s oath/declaration; IDS with a statement compliant with § 1.704(d); resubmission of unlocatable previously filed papers (§ 1.251); requests for acknowledgement of an IDS meeting § 1.97/1.98 conditions if timely requested; comments on substance of applicant-initiated interview that resulted in allowance; letters related to government interests). Papers that WILL be treated as failures include: amendment under § 1.312; paper containing a claim for priority/benefit or request to correct priority/benefit information (e.g., ADS to correct foreign priority); request for corrected filing receipt; certified copy of priority document; drawings; letters re biologic deposits; requests to change/correct inventorship; and IDS not accompanied by a statement in compliance with § 1.704(d). The MPEP also notes changes in practice (e.g., status inquiries, refund requests, inventor’s oath now generally not treated as failures due to electronic filing/processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file compliant appeal brief within three months (37 CFR 1.704(c)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: For appeals where the notice of appeal was filed on or after Sep 17, 2012, failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 within three months from the date the notice of appeal to the PTAB was filed (35 U.S.C. 134 and 37 CFR 41.31) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the appeal brief is due within two months under § 41.37, § 1.704(c)(11) provides a three‑month window before PTA is reduced. If a non‑compliant brief is filed and a compliant brief is later filed within three months, no PTA reduction occurs; if the compliant brief is filed more than three months after the notice of appeal, PTA may be reduced. PTA reduced by days beginning the day after three months from the notice of appeal filing and ending on the date a compliant appeal brief or an RCE filed in compliance with § 1.114 was filed. If the Office reopens prosecution more than three months after the notice of appeal but prior to submission of a compliant brief, that reopened period will not be treated as applicant delay under § 1.704(c)(11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a request for continued examination (RCE) after notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.704(c)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for RCEs filed on or after March 10, 2015, submission of a request for continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 has been mailed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the mailing date of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) was filed. This prevents applicants from obtaining additional PTA by removing an application from the issue process after allowance. The MPEP explains that RCEs filed after allowance remove the application from issue processing and require PTO resources to reexamine the application.
